content: Globulin is one of the two primary types of serum proteins, the other being albumin. This term refers to a diverse group of protein families that are characterized by their larger molecular size and lower solubility in pure water compared to albumin. During serum electrophoresis, globulins migrate less than albumin. The term globulin is sometimes used interchangeably with globular protein. However, it is important to note that while albumin is a globular protein, it is not classified as a globulin. All other globular proteins found in serum, apart from albumin, are considered globulins.
